name: 31. Gemini/Vertex mediaResolution honored, request-level and per-part (image prompt tokens)
description:
Regression: generationConfig.mediaResolution was silently dropped in the Gemini -> Bifrost -> Gemini
Responses conversion on the /genai generateContent path, so a Vertex/Gemini image request billed the
model-default image token count regardless of MEDIA_RESOLUTION_LOW/HIGH (e.g. ~1290 instead of ~74
prompt tokens for a 1024x1024 image). thinkingConfig survived because both conversion legs handle it;
mediaResolution was handled by neither.

Fix: round mediaResolution through ExtraParams["media_resolution"] in core/providers/gemini
(convertGenerationConfigToResponsesParameters inbound + convertParamsToGenerationConfigResponses outbound).

The only external signal is usageMetadata.promptTokenCount, so each pair sends the SAME 1024x1024 image
(folder-level prerequest sets {{mediaResImage}}) and asserts the HIGH request reports more prompt tokens
than the LOW request. If the field is dropped, both fall back to the same default => equal counts =>
the HIGH-exceeds-LOW assertion fails, independent of what the model default is. 31.1/31.2 pin the fix on
the GenAI route (needs only {{genaiKey}}); 31.3/31.4 pin the same invariant on Vertex (the reported
route) and skip cleanly if Vertex is not configured.

31.5-31.9 pin the second, separate half: Google also models media resolution per Part (Vertex AI v1 Part field 12), and the per-part value overrides generationConfig for that part. Bifrost's Part type had no such field and Part.UnmarshalJSON decodes into a closed alias, so the key was discarded at parse time -- before any of the conversion work 31.1-31.4 cover. Reported against v1.6.7: an ULTRA_HIGH image billed ~21.0k prompt tokens through /genai versus ~22.1k direct, while /genai with x-model-provider: gemini and /genai_passthrough both matched Google, because those forward raw bytes instead of converting. Per-part is Gemini 3 only, so these cases hardcode gemini-3.6-flash rather than using {{genaiModel}}/{{vertexModel}}. 31.5 sends the snake_case media_resolution spelling Google's own REST reference documents; 31.6-31.9 send camelCase. 31.7 and 31.9 are the ones that pin the override semantics: generationConfig says LOW while the part says HIGH, and the part must win.

That override shape is required rather than cosmetic on the HIGH cases. Google documents Gemini 3 image tokens as low 280 / medium 560 / high 1120 / ultra_high 2240, with the unspecified default also 1120 (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/media-resolution). Default and HIGH are therefore indistinguishable, so a bare per-part HIGH case cannot tell "HIGH honored" from "field dropped". Pinning generationConfig to LOW makes a dropped per-part field fall back to ~280 instead of ~1120, which the HIGH-exceeds-LOW assertion then catches.
